title: Double a Number Represented as a Linked List
description:
You are given the `head` of a non-empty singly linked list representing a non-negative integer without leading zeros (except for the number `0` itself), with the **most significant digit** at `head`.

Return the `head` of the linked list after doubling the represented integer. Aim for `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^4].
The number has no leading zeros except for 0 itself.
hints: Reversing the list, doubling each digit with carry, and reversing back solves the problem in O(n) time and O(1) space.
Alternatively, observe that doubling any digit `d` produces a carry of `1` into the left neighbor if and only if `d >= 5` (since `2*4 + 1 = 9 < 10`), enabling a single left-to-right pass.
